summary.headline: Awfis FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR1,493 crore and EBITDA 37% to INR550 crore, with FY27 guided to 25-27% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Awfis reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR1,493 crore (up 24% YoY) and operating EBITDA of INR550 crore (up 37%, margin 36.8%), with PAT before exceptionals up 66% to INR71 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR410 crore (up 21%) with EBITDA of INR152 crore (margin 37%). The company deliberately slowed seat additions to focus on Grade A/A+ premium centers, with gross seat additions of about 30,000 and net addition of about 22,000 in FY26. Design and build (Transform) revenue was softer, though its third-party business grew.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR11 crore in Q4 FY25 (+107%)

financial_highlights.value: INR655 crore before tax; INR616 crore net operating cash flow; normalized INR216 crore
Net cash through FY26; net debt to equity -0.20; gross debt to equity 0.09

segments.name: Coworking and allied services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,237 crore (+35% YoY); Q4 revenue INR342 crore (+27% YoY, +6% QoQ). Management said it met both revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY26.

segments.name: Awfis Transform (design and build)
segments.commentary: FY26 softer on project timing and fewer managed aggregation deals. Third-party revenue rose from INR95 crore (FY25) to INR152 crore (FY26), with third-party share at 59% (from 47%). Net D&B margin about 7-8%. INR130 crore of mandates won for delivery over the next 6-7 months.

segments.name: Frame by Awfis (furniture)
segments.commentary: Capex-light contract manufacturing across 5+ partners. Majority of new coworking centers to deploy Frame furniture by H1 FY27; 2-3 large external mandates targeted by H2 FY27.

segments.name: Others (facility management)
segments.commentary: Line item reflects the facility management business sold in September 2024; management does not expect further revenue from it.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 25-27%: coworking and allied 25-27% and Awfis Transform 22-25%.
FY27 gross seat additions guided at 22,000-25,000 seats (about 1.25 million sq ft), with capex broadly similar to FY26 levels for these seats.
Managed aggregation to stay around 60% of supply, with straight lease about 40%.
Mature-center occupancy (84%) targeted to rise by at least 100 bps over the next couple of quarters.
Margin expansion expected over 2-3 years from premiumization and a higher third-party share in D&B; no numeric margin target given.
Partial managed office and developer partnership pipelines expected to be meaningful supply pillars in FY27-FY28.
capex_capacity: Supply at FY26 end: 250 centers and about 167,000 seats in 18 cities; signed supply 266 centers and about 184,000 seats; operational capacity about 156,000-157,000 seats.
FY26 gross additions about 30,000 seats across 41 new centers, all in Grade A/A+; net addition about 22,000 seats after about 8,000 seats closed.
35 Gold and Elite centers at FY26 end (27 Gold, 8 Elite); premium footprint covers 8 GCC hubs including all 7 Tier 1 cities.
Partial managed office centers targeted at 30,000-50,000 sq ft; some deals up to 65,000-70,000 sq ft with 40-50% day-1 client demand.
Advanced talks with 2 institutional developers on partnerships with shared capex; over 4 lakh sq ft pre-committed under the MA model through Q2 FY28.
Awfis 6.0 design refresh expected to carry capex similar to 5.0 per seat; 6.0 to be the majority of seats added.
demand_pricing: Enterprise and MNC clients 64% of client base; average client tenure 37 months; lock-in tenure 26 months.
500-plus seat cohort 37% of portfolio; 48% of clients operate across multiple centers; clients in 10+ centers up 600 bps QoQ.
Blended occupancy 76% (up 300 bps over last four quarters on average seat base above 145,000); mature centers (over 12 months) 84%.
100-plus GCC clients across 9 cities contributing about 23% of rental revenue; 14 major GCC mandates closed in FY26, 6 already committed for FY27.
Revenue-to-rent ratio about 2.3x; revenue to gross fixed assets 1.5x.
Sold over 58,000 seats in FY26. Rent escalations: fixed for first 3 years, then 15% escalation per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross seat additions appear to be 26,000 when the sum of quarterly guidance was lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross additions were about 30,000 seats, with about 8,000 closed, giving a net addition of about 22,000 (157,000 operational seats vs about 135,000 a year earlier). Seat additions were kept low by a focus on quality over quantity.

qa_highlights.question: Will premiumization be a one-time shift, and what growth should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said premiumization is now the default and non-negotiable, not a one-time step. Growth is driven by realization per seat, with FY27 revenue guided at about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin profile of D&B and the revenue-to-rent ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: D&B net margins are about 7-8%. Revenue-to-rent ratio is about 2.3x.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in lease principal payments in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the 30,000 seats added in FY26 and late-FY25 centers coming off rent-free periods, plus renewal escalations. No average escalation percentage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the approximately 5% seat closure rate in FY26 a normal churn level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 was a portfolio rebalancing year. About 3,000 seats were a single-client short-term setup, and the rest were exits at renewal or from older buildings below the Grade A+ bar. Management said 5% is not the churn rate it expects going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the gap between normalized rent and cash-flow rent widened?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the reconciling items from H1 persist, mainly operating lease items, which grow with time. He offered a one-on-one walkthrough and gave no quantified explanation on the call.

risks_watch: Lease principal outflows are rising with seat additions, rent-free expiries and renewal escalations; the cash-rent reconciliation gap widened to about INR60 crore in FY26 from about INR20 crore in H1.
Blended occupancy of 76% is dragged by ramping new centers; the 100 bps mature-cohort target is still to be delivered.
Seat additions of 22,000-25,000 in FY27 are well below the earlier 40,000 seat guidance, which was reduced in the quarter.
Design and build growth has been soft, and FY27 guidance of 22-25% depends on the INR130 crore order book converting.
Developer partnerships with 2 institutional developers are in advanced discussions but not signed.
Frame by Awfis is at an early stage, with external mandate targets for H2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategy and FY26 delivery, with consistent emphasis on premiumization and ROCE. Less forthcoming on seat-addition reconciliation and the cash-rent gap, which management deferred to one-on-one follow-ups. Corrected its own FY27 guidance ranges for coworking and D&B during the call.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a defining year for Awfis. It was a year marked by strong execution, deeper enterprise adoption, sharper premiumization of the network and disciplined capital deployment.
Premiumization has now become default at Awfis, not a strategy overlay.
So the seat addition still is 30,000. It's because of some of the closures that have happened.
Yes. 5% is not the kind of a churn which we would look at.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 25-27% (coworking 25-27%, Transform 22-25%), backed by 22-25k gross seat additions (~1.25m sq ft) and 4 lakh+ sq ft pre-committed under MA model, plus INR130 crore of D&B mandates, though no capex-to-seat figures beyond 'similar to FY26' and no order-book quantification for the coworking side.
